criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The mission concept identifies a clear Australian beneficiary and user base, explaining the importance of monitoring coral bleaching on the Great Barrier Reef. The rationale is justified using relevant context. However, it lacks specific engineering requirements, such as defined revisit rates, coverage area constraints, or resolution requirements.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A Gantt chart is included along with task breakdowns mapping to mission phases like launch, orbit, communications, and end-of-life. However, the plan lacks robust risk management, dependencies, and contingency pathways beyond a general buffer week.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: No actual engineering results, trade studies, preliminary orbital parameters, or simulation outputs are presented. Merely completing software tutorials and conducting background reading does not provide tangible preliminary technical progress on the mission design itself.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, in my progress, I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: The report has a logical structure, readable prose, and a clean Gantt chart graphic. However, referencing is informal, relying on raw URLs in both the footnotes and the final links list rather than standard academic citation formats.

technical_issues.issue: Lacks quantified engineering requirements such as target spatial resolution, spectral bands, revisit frequency, and operational swath width for reef monitoring.
No preliminary orbital parameters (e.g. altitude, inclination, repetition cycle) or astrodynamics calculations are provided to demonstrate technical design progress.
References are listed as bare URLs without standard bibliographical metadata (authors, titles, publication dates).

overall: The mission rationale is well-motivated and the project plan is laid out clearly via a Gantt chart. However, the submission lacks technical engineering progress, offering no preliminary orbital calculations or simulation outputs, and citations should follow proper academic conventions.

feedback.summary: You have established a compelling, well-motivated mission concept addressing coral bleaching on the Great Barrier Reef, supported by a structured Gantt chart. To advance your mission design, focus on translating your user needs into quantified technical requirements, performing baseline astrodynamics and orbital calculations, and formatting all citations according to standard academic conventions.
next_steps: Calculate baseline orbital parameters (such as altitude, inclination, and repeat cycle) to show concrete technical progress on mission design.
Define explicit engineering requirements in your concept section, specifying target ground spatial resolution, spectral bands, and operational swath width.
Convert all raw URL links in your footnotes and Useful Links section into standard academic citations with full metadata.

criteria.C1: In Mission Concept & Rationale, you clearly identified Australian beneficiaries and justified the need for coral reef monitoring. To reach Accomplished, specify quantified engineering requirements derived from these user needs, such as required ground spatial resolution, coverage swath width, spectral bands, and specific revisit frequencies.
criteria.C2: In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, your Gantt chart (Image 1) effectively breaks down key mission phases. To reach Accomplished, make your plan more robust by detailing task dependencies, identifying critical path risks, and establishing explicit contingency pathways rather than relying solely on a single buffer week.
criteria.C3: In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, your background reading and tutorial work demonstrate good preparation. However, to reach Adequate or Accomplished, you must include actual engineering outputs, such as preliminary orbital parameter calculations (altitude, inclination, repeat cycle), sensor trade studies, or preliminary simulation data with brief technical interpretation.
criteria.C4: Your report features a logical structure, clear headings, and clean visual presentation in your Gantt chart. To achieve Accomplished, replace raw URLs in your footnotes and the Useful Links section with consistent, formal academic citations containing full bibliographical metadata, including authors, publication titles, and dates.
